inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation add-back ($401M). HCA publishes no combined equity-award figure and tags no separate net-share-settlement tax withholding line, so the add-back is used as the full SBC charge. Interest income is immaterial (net-debt company) and set to 0.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $10,067M; H1 2026 $3,635M. Buybacks far exceed SBC (~25x), so the flat share count is fully funded; the count actually falls ~8-10%/yr, which the flat-count convention treats as value-neutral (buyback cash and debt capacity are fungible).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 216.50M basic on the Q2 2026 10-Q cover (late July 2026, filed 2026-07-28) plus 2.29M dilutive securities (Q2 2026 weighted diluted 222.83M less basic 220.54M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet at 2026-06-30: LongTermDebtNoncurrent 43,454 + DebtCurrent 6,264 = 49,718 total debt, less cash 1,013. NOTE: the DB total_debt column (52,905 at Q1 2026) adds us-gaap:LongTermDebt (which already contains the current portion) to DebtCurrent and so double-counts ~$4-5B; the correct Q1 2026 figure is 39,491 + 8,532 = 48,023. Operating lease liabilities (~$2.2B) are excluded from net debt because operating lease cost (~$516M/yr) is already an expense inside EBITDA under ASC 842.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Cost of equity ~9.2% (10y UST ~4.2%, beta ~1.0 for a policy-exposed hospital operator, ERP 5%); pre-tax cost of debt 4.9% (FY2025 interest expense $2,248M on ~$46B average debt), 3.8% after tax; market weights ~66% equity / 34% net debt at the current price. Market-implied WACC ~7.4%, rounded UP to 8.0% because a 5% ERP on a beta of 1.0 understates the equity risk of a business whose reimbursement is set administratively for ~45% of revenue. This is the single place risk is charged in the rate; the scenarios carry the policy risk in the flows and all three use the same 8.0%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842) are an operating expense inside EBITDA (OperatingLeaseCost $516M FY2025); operating lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. HCA consolidates hospital joint ventures with large noncontrolling interests (NCI net income $998M FY2025, $468M H1 2026; NCI distributions $827M FY2025). The NCI profit share is deducted inside the EBITDA margin path: FY2025 consolidated EBITDA 15,603 (ProfitLoss 7,782 + tax 2,050 + interest 2,248 + D&A 3,523; ties to company Adjusted EBITDA within rounding) + SBC 401 - NCI 998 = 15,006 attributable pre-SBC EBITDA = 19.85% of revenue. Calibration: FY0 component NOPAT 8,511 vs reported attributable NI 6,784 + after-tax interest 1,726 = 8,510. No NCI deduction in the bridge (would charge it twice).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, US hospital operator) with two adaptations from owner-fcf-adaptations.md: (c) minority interests folded into an attributable EBITDA margin, and (b) leases as operating cost. NEGATIVE BOOK EQUITY (-$6.6B at 2026-06-30) is a deliberate leveraged capital structure from the 2006 LBO and ~$50B of cumulative debt-funded buybacks, not distress: EBITDA/interest 6.9x, EBIT/interest 5.4x, net debt/EBITDA 3.1x, BBB-range credit. It is handled, not treated as a data error: (1) the equity CAGR is meaningless (negative to negative) so the growth anchor is the revenue CAGR tempered by the ACA/OBBBA headwind, not book value; (2) the DCF is unlevered (EBIT -> NOPAT -> unlevered FCF at WACC) with net debt deducted once in the bridge, so book equity never enters; (3) because net debt is ~34% of EV, per-share value is ~1.5x as sensitive to EV as an unlevered peer, which the sensitivity grid makes visible. FY0 = FY2025 actuals; Y1 = FY2026 (guidance: revenue $77.0-79.5B, Adjusted EBITDA $15.4-16.1B, capex $5.0-5.5B; H1 2026 revenue +6.5%). last_fcf follows the contract (reported FCF - SBC - interest income = 7,291) but is a LEVERED, CONSOLIDATED figure inflated by FY2025 cash-tax timing (taxes paid 1,740 vs 2,050 expensed; H1 2026 taxes paid 725 vs 146) and working capital; the component-built FY0 unlevered attributable owner FCF is ~7,170 and that, not 7,291, is what the projection compounds from. Cash tax 22.5% (23.2% book rate on attributable pre-tax income; permanent 100% bonus depreciation under OBBBA keeps the cash rate slightly below book). Working capital captured at -3% of revenue growth (receivables-heavy; growth consumes cash). Terminal cap 18x FCF for base/bull (~8.4x consolidated EBITDA, in line with HCA's own 8-10x history) and 15x for bear. Historical FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF (post-SBC) series; the 3-year figure is distorted by the FY2022 trough and FY2025 peak and is not used as an anchor.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Revenue CAGR (8% 3y/5y) haircut for the FY2026-28 ACA subsidy lapse and OBBBA Medicaid headwinds; equity CAGR is undefined because shareholders' equity is negative throughout (FY2020-21 briefly positive), a consequence of debt-funded buybacks rather than value destruction. EPS CAGR (14-21%) is inflated by the ~30% share-count reduction over five years and is not a growth anchor.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR not computable (negative book equity from LBO-era capital structure); EPS CAGR diverges >30% from revenue CAGR because of buybacks. Revenue CAGR used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2020 6,035; FY2021 4,942; FY2022 3,786; FY2023 4,425; FY2024 5,279; FY2025 7,291. FY2020 is inflated by CARES Act advances and FY2025 by cash-tax timing and working capital, so the 5-year owner-FCF CAGR of 3.9% understates the underlying trend (~6-7%) and the 3-year figure of 24.4% overstates it. SBC is only ~0.5% of revenue and has fallen from 0.75% (FY2021), so the owner and reported CAGRs are within 1pp of each other.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Attributable pre-SBC EBITDA margin (consolidated EBITDA + SBC - NCI profit share). FY2025 actual 19.85%. Y1 19.3% = FY2026 guidance midpoint ($15.75B consolidated on ~$78.6B) + SBC ~0.45% - NCI ~1.2%. Y2-Y3 dip to 18.7% as OBBBA work requirements (2027) and provider-tax phase-down (2028+) bite; recovery to 19.0% by Y7 as cost actions, commercial rate resets and outpatient mix offset, never back to the FY2025 peak.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guidance $5.0-5.5B = 6.7% of revenue; ~$7B of approved projects come online over two years, then growth capex moderates toward 6.0% with D&A rising to 5.2% behind it.

scenario_narratives.base: The ACA enhanced-subsidy lapse and OBBBA Medicaid provisions play out roughly as management now models: the exchange-to-uninsured conversion stays near one-for-one, so FY2026 attributable EBITDA margin falls ~55bp from the FY2025 peak, and the steeper OBBBA effects (work requirements from 2027, provider-tax phase-down from 2028) take another 60bp over FY2027-28 before cost actions, commercial rate resets and the outpatient mix shift claw ~30bp back by the end of the decade. Volume stays healthy (record 73% occupancy, ~$7B of approved capacity coming online, Sun Belt demographics), so revenue compounds at 3.5-4.5% through the headwind and slows to 3% by year 10. Capex runs at the guided $5.0-5.5B and moderates to 6% of revenue; the company keeps buying back stock, which the flat-count convention treats as value-neutral. Terminal value bound by the 18x FCF cap (~8.4x consolidated EBITDA, HCA's own trading range).
scenario_narratives.bull: Congress extends or partially restores the enhanced ACA premium tax credits before the 2027-28 cliff, or the uninsured shift stabilises at the FY2026 level; states re-engineer supplemental payment programmes around the provider-tax caps so Medicaid revenue holds; commercial payers accept mid-single-digit rate increases and the outpatient buildout (20 sites per hospital by 2030) lifts attributable margin back to 20% by year 6. The $7B capacity programme converts record occupancy into 5-5.5% revenue growth through FY2030, capex tapers toward 5.8% as the programme matures, and terminal growth is 3%. Same 8% WACC; the upside is in the flows, not the rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: The uninsured shift persists at one-for-one and a softer labour market pushes commercial mix down; OBBBA work requirements and redeterminations cut Medicaid enrolment harder than modelled, the provider-tax phase-down removes most supplemental payment revenue by 2030, and clinical labour inflation stays above pricing. Attributable margin falls ~285bp to 17% by FY2028 and never recovers, revenue growth stalls at 2-3% as management trims growth capex, and the terminal multiple compresses to 15x FCF (~7x consolidated EBITDA). Refinancing ~$5-6B/yr of maturities at higher coupons does not threaten solvency (EBITDA/interest still >5x) but, with net debt at a third of EV, every 1% of EV lost is ~1.5% of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the dominant swing factor is a single regulator (federal ACA/Medicaid policy) that has already moved against the company twice in twelve months, and management's own conversion-rate model was wrong by ~20 points in FY2026; the steepest OBBBA effects are still ahead (2027-28). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right (a Congressional subsidy fix and state workarounds to the provider-tax caps) on top of flawless execution of the capacity programme. Base 50%: the demand side (occupancy, demographics, capacity) is not in doubt; the payer-mix side is.

valuation_philosophy.summary: HCA is valued as an unlevered owner-FCF stream on an attributable (post-NCI), post-SBC basis, discounted at 8% with net debt of ~$48.7B deducted once. The business is a scale-advantaged, demographically supported cash generator whose near-term earnings are being set by federal policy rather than demand: the ACA subsidy lapse and OBBBA Medicaid changes are a multi-year margin headwind, not a one-quarter event, and the scenarios differ mainly on how much of the ~20% attributable EBITDA margin survives it. Negative book equity is a financing choice (LBO legacy plus ~$50B of buybacks) and is irrelevant to the DCF, but the leverage it reflects makes the equity ~1.5x as sensitive to enterprise value as an unlevered peer: the sensitivity grid, not the base case, is the honest picture. The terminal value is capped at 18x unlevered FCF (~8.4x EBITDA), inside HCA's own historical range, so no re-rating is assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: Federal policy: the ACA enhanced-subsidy lapse (already $1.0-1.2B of FY2026 EBITDA) and OBBBA Medicaid work requirements and provider-tax phase-down (steepest in 2027-28) could take margins below the bear path if the uninsured shift compounds with a recession.

Leverage: net debt is ~34% of enterprise value, so a 10% change in EV is a ~15% change in equity value; refinancing ~$5-6B/yr of maturities at higher coupons erodes the equity share even though solvency is not in question.
Terminal weight: roughly 60% of enterprise value is terminal; the 18x cap holds the exit at ~8.4x EBITDA, but a structurally lower hospital multiple (7x, as in the bear case) removes ~$60/share.
NCI leakage: joint-venture partners take ~6% of EBITDA; if new capacity is JV-funded the attributable share of growth is lower than the consolidated numbers suggest.
Labour: nursing and physician cost inflation above commercial rate increases compresses margin independently of policy; contract-labour reliance rose again in 2025-26.
